title: Analyzing Why |x| + |y| = 1 and |x + y| = 1 Are Not Functions of x
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Vertical Line Test
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graphs of the equations (a) |x| + |y| = 1 and (b) |x + y| = 1, and explain why neither is the graph of a function of x.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) Diamond } y = \pm(1 - |x|) \text{ on } [-1, 1]; \quad \text{(b) Parallel lines } y = -x \pm 1; \quad \text{Both fail the Vertical Line Test}

steps.title: Analyze Equation (a): |x| + |y| = 1
steps.explanation: Since |y| >= 0, solutions exist for |x| <= 1, i.e., -1 <= x <= 1. The graph is a diamond (a square tilted by 45 degrees) with vertices at (1, 0), (0, 1), (-1, 0), and (0, -1).
steps.why: In each of the four quadrants, |x| + |y| = 1 reduces to a linear segment connecting adjacent axes intercepts.

steps.title: Show That Equation (a) Fails the Vertical Line Test
steps.explanation: For every x strictly between -1 and 1, 1 - |x| > 0, so there are two distinct y-values of opposite sign. Every vertical line in (-1, 1) intersects the diamond twice.
steps.why: Having two distinct y-values for each x in (-1, 1) violates the definition of a function of x.

steps.title: Analyze Equation (b): |x + y| = 1 and Show Failure
steps.mathExpression: |x + y| = 1 \iff x + y = 1 \text{ or } x + y = -1 \iff y = 1 - x \text{ or } y = -1 - x
steps.explanation: The equation |x + y| = 1 splits into two parallel lines of slope -1: y = -x + 1 and y = -x - 1. For every real number x, a vertical line intersects both parallel lines, yielding two outputs y for each x.
steps.why: Every vertical line x = c intersects two distinct non-vertical parallel lines in two distinct points.
